v: For you are my hope, Lord GOD, my confidence from my youth.
b: Almost everyone has known moments of disappointment in life, but we are to learn to place our hope wholly in the LORD God.

In Psalm 71:5, the psalmist tells us that the LORD is his hope, and that he has trusted in God since his youth. We can learn from the psalmist's example and place our hope wholly in the Lord. When we meet setbacks and disappointment, we should not lose heart, but ask God for help and strength, because God is always with us. Whenever we face the many challenges and difficulties of life, we can remember this verse and be confident that the LORD is our hope. He will keep us and hold us up at all times, so that we do not fall.

Let us consider a story. There was a little girl whose physical disability kept her from running and playing freely like other children. But from a young age she learned to place her hope wholly in the LORD, and whenever she felt tired or defeated, she asked God for help and strength. She believed that God would help her overcome every difficulty and become someone who could contribute something for Him. One day she took part in a sports competition for people with disabilities. Facing competitors who were eager to win, she showed her own strength and in the end won the race. At that moment her heart was full of thanks and joy, because she knew that she had achieved this not by her own power but through God's help and blessing.

This story tells us that whatever challenges and difficulties we face, if we place our hope wholly in the LORD, we will receive God's help and strength. God will help us overcome every difficulty and make us His witnesses in the world, so that our lives may show forth His lovingkindness and grace.
pr: Dear LORD, thank You that You are our hope. May our lives always rest in Your embrace. When we face challenges and difficulties, give us strength and wisdom to overcome them. Fill our hearts with faith, hope and love, and let our lives show forth Your glory and goodness.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May God be your hope, and may God's grace be with you. Amen.

v: My soul, wait in silence for God alone, for my expectation is from him.
b: In life we often meet many challenges and difficulties that leave us confused and at a loss. But in Psalm 62:5 the psalmist tells us that when we feel helpless, we should wait on God with our whole heart, because our hope comes from God.

Hope comes from God. This was the psalmist's deep insight. In our daily lives, many people face unemployment, family problems, health problems and other challenges, and feel lost and powerless. But the psalmist teaches us to wait on God in silence. This does not mean giving up control of our lives; it means putting our trust in God's hands, believing that He will lead us out of our trouble.

There was a young girl named Kathy who lost her parents when she was very small and was taken in by relatives. But in her teens she unexpectedly lost her adoptive family as well and had to face life alone. For Kathy this was an extremely hard time, and she did not know what to do. But Kathy did not give up hope. She held firmly to her belief in the existence and great power of God.

Kathy began to read the Bible and pray earnestly, and she found a small group in a church where she could share her experiences and faith with other Christians. During this time Kathy found that her life was being changed in remarkable ways. Her faith and hope were rekindled, and she could see a brighter tomorrow. In the end God prepared a job for her and led her to meet a good man, and the two began a happy life together. Kathy knew that all of this came from God's grace and blessing.

This story tells us that no matter how many challenges and difficulties we face, if we believe in God and wait calmly for His help, He will surely bring us the best solution. Let us be like Kathy: read the Bible and pray earnestly, find a community of Christians, and share and fellowship among them. That way we will have more support and help around us, and our faith and hope in God will grow.
pr: Dear Lord, thank You that You are our hope. When we feel weak and helpless, give us firm faith and hope, so that we may wait earnestly for Your help and guidance. Give us wisdom and courage to face the challenges and difficulties of life, and let our faith grow ever firmer in Your grace and power. Give us hearts that love one another, so that we care for each other and become a blessing to each other. Finally, we ask You to bless us and our families, and under Your keeping and guidance to let us walk the right path and carry out Your good plan. In the name of the Lord Jesus I bless you: may you wait on God with all your heart, may your hope come from God, and may God's grace be with you. Amen.

v: The LORD takes pleasure in those who fear him, in those who hope in his loving kindness.
b: In this passage God tells us that He delights in those who revere Him and who trust that He will show grace and lovingkindness. Such people have hope, because they believe in God's good purposes and trust that His promises will never fail.

In life we may face all kinds of setbacks and difficulties that make us feel we have lost hope. But if we turn our eyes to God and believe His word, we can draw strength from this hope. As the Bible says, even though we face trials in the world, through hope we can receive endurance and comfort.

We can take inspiration from the story of a legendary basketball coach. When he was very young he dreamed of becoming a professional basketball player, but for various reasons he could not realize that dream. Yet he did not lose hope. Instead he turned to coaching and became an outstanding coach. Under his leadership his team achieved remarkable things and set many records.

This coach's story tells us that even if our plans change, we can still have hope and trust that God will lead us toward a better future. As Psalm 147:11 says, when we fear God and trust His promises and lovingkindness, we receive His pleasure and blessing.
Let us give thanks together for God's lovingkindness and hope, and may His grace and blessing always be with us.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you on this day full of hope and love, that you may be blessed and become a witness who passes on God's truth and love. Amen!

v: through whom we also have our access by faith into this grace in which we stand. We rejoice in hope of the glory of God.
b: Hope is a beautiful quality that every Christian must have. We should always hold faith and hope in God, so that through the ups and downs of life we can keep our joy and peace. Take a sister named Li Hong. At work she met many setbacks and difficulties, but she was always able to stay positive and steadfast, because she believed God would lead her through these hard times and let her experience His lovingkindness and faithfulness in the midst of the challenges.

When we have hope in God, we can not only get through hardship but also look forward with joy to meeting the Lord in eternal life and experiencing His boundless glory. As the Bible says: “Hope doesn’t disappoint us, because God’s love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit who was given to us.” (Romans 5:5)

Let us do as the apostle Paul taught: enter by faith into the grace God has given us, and rejoice with gladness in the hope of God's glory. If we believe in God's love, faithfulness and promises, we can live lives full of hope and faith at every moment.

In our daily lives we may meet setbacks, difficulties or disappointments, but when we have hope in God, we can be like a Christian called Brother Zhang. He once faced challenges at work and major decisions in life, yet he was always able to keep his faith and hope. He said, “God has already given us the best of grace, and He will continue to lead us forward.” These words are moving, because his faith and hope show his trust in and reliance on God.
Finally, let us turn our eyes to the glory of God, the wonderful future for which we hope. May we be like the apostle Paul, who rejoiced in faith in the hope of the glory of God.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you that you may keep growing in faith and be filled with joy and peace in hope. Amen!

v: For we were saved in hope, but hope that is seen is not hope. For who hopes for that which he sees?
b: Dear brothers and sisters, in our life of faith hope is a very important part. When we believe in the Lord Jesus, we also believe in His promises and in His return. This conviction gives us a mighty hope that leads us, each day, in the hope God has given.
But this hope is not built on what we see. Such things are temporary and unreliable, whereas our hope is built on our Lord Jesus Christ, who is eternal and dependable.

There is a story about a young man who wanted to cross a chasm but was afraid, because he knew that below was a dark and unfathomable abyss. He asked an old man what to do, and the old man threw down a rope and told him, “You only need to trust this rope. It will hold you firmly and lead you across the chasm.” This is like our faith: we trust the Lord Jesus Christ as our Savior and hope, and we must put all our confidence in Him, for nothing is more dependable and steadfast than He is.

Besides this, Romans 8:28 tells us: “We know that all things work together for good for those who love God.” This means that even when hardship and adversity come into our lives, these things are for our good, because God teaches us through them, helps us grow, and in the end accomplishes His good plan. This is also part of our hope: even in difficulty, we know that God loves us and will lead us through our lives.

Our faith and hope are not only about ourselves; they can also affect the lives of others. When we live out our faith, live out the life of Jesus, and let God's love shine in our lives, we can become hope for others as well. There is a true story of a woman who fell ill in a hospital. A neighbor who visited her asked whether she had hope for the future, and she answered, “My hope is not built here; my hope is built on the Lord Jesus Christ.” Through her faith and hope this woman gave others great encouragement and hope. So when we live out our faith and hold on to hope, we too can touch the lives of others and become their hope and support.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May the Lord give you more faith, hope and love, so that you can stand firm in the faith and face the challenges and opportunities of life with courage. May God's grace and peace be with you always. Amen.

v: For we through the Spirit, by faith wait for the hope of righteousness.
b: When we trust the Holy Spirit and wait by faith, we can wait for the righteousness we hope for. What does “righteousness” mean here? In the Bible, “righteousness” stands for God's justice and moral standard, and also for our relationship with God. When we believe in God and receive the salvation of Jesus Christ, we are justified by faith; that is, we become children of God and enter into an intimate relationship with Him.

But this is not the end. We must still keep relying on the Spirit and wait by faith for the fuller righteousness to come. In this world we are often struck by setbacks and difficulties that leave us in despair and loss. But when we believe God's word and have a steady relationship with Him, we can see these setbacks and difficulties as opportunities God uses to train us.

There was a young man named Tom who had a great dream: to become a professional pool player. But in the beginning he met many setbacks, and the number of matches he lost far exceeded the number he won. This left Tom in despair and loss, and he even wanted to give up his dream.

But Tom did not give up. He learned from each failure and kept improving his skills and his mindset. He kept believing in his ability and believing that his dream could come true. In the end, after a long and arduous journey, Tom became an outstanding professional pool player and even won several international championships.

This story tells us that when we face setbacks and failure, we should not give up hope and dreams. Believe in your ability, and keep relying on the Spirit and waiting by faith for the righteousness we hope for. God and His plan will never let us down. When we put our trust in Him, we can see His wonderful plan in our lives.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May your faith stand firm as you wait for the righteousness you hope for, may your hope grow brighter under God's leading, and may your love grow mature and rich in God's love. Amen.

v: in hope of eternal life, which God, who can’t lie, promised before time began;
b: In this passage the author of Titus leads us to hope for the eternal life promised by the God who does not lie. Sometimes we may feel lost, afraid and helpless, not knowing what the future will hold, but if we have the hope of eternal life, it becomes a pillar in our hearts and helps us through hard times.

We can find inspiration in a song titled “Your Grace Is Sufficient for Me.” In the song, the writer says that when his faith grows small, he will trust that God's grace is enough to hold him up, because true hope is found in God's grace. As Titus says, we should hope in the God who does not lie, believing that before the ages began He promised us eternal life. Whatever difficulty or danger we face, we can rely on this hope and be kept safe under His protection.

In daily life we can also find many examples of this kind of hope. A farmer sows seed in spring, hoping for a bountiful harvest in autumn; a newborn baby, after nine months of waiting, finally comes into the world, with a future of growth and development ahead; a person works hard, hoping for promotion and success. These examples tell us that in life hope is what drives and sustains us, and gives us courage to face the challenges ahead.
Finally, let us return once more to the truth of Scripture. As Christians, we can believe what Titus says: that before the ages began the God who does not lie promised us eternal life.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May this hope be a pillar in your life, giving you faith, hope and love, so that you rely on God and face every challenge. May the hope of the Lord God fill your life. Amen.

v: that being justified by his grace, we might be made heirs according to the hope of eternal life.
b: This verse reminds us that through the redeeming grace of the Lord Jesus we can receive the hope of eternal life and become heirs of God, that is, children of God. This hope cannot be compared with all the wealth and pleasure of the world; it gives our souls eternal peace, joy and contentment.

How, then, can we receive this hope? We need to believe in the Lord Jesus Christ and obediently follow His way. When we entrust ourselves to God and take His will as our goal, our lives become fuller and richer, and we will have greater hope and confidence.

It is like a farmer, who must first plow, sow and water before he can expect a harvest. In the same way, when we rely on God and act according to His will, our lives begin to reap abundant fruit. That fruit is the hope of eternal life.

We can also understand the value of the hope of eternal life from moving stories. There was once a famous musician who suffered from an incurable disease, and the doctors told him he had only a few months to live. Yet he did not give up on life; instead he worked even harder at composing and performing music. He dedicated these works to God, and believed that his soul would enter heaven and receive the hope of eternal life. The day before he left this world, he wrote a heartfelt letter telling all who loved him that he was ready, because he knew his soul was about to enter heaven and enjoy the hope of eternal life.

This musician's story helps us see deeply that only by believing in the Lord Jesus Christ can we receive the true hope of eternal life. When we follow His way and entrust ourselves wholly into His hands, we can enjoy this hope and have a wonderful future.
pr: We ask the Lord to give us faith, hope and love, so that in daily life we follow His will and hold fast to the hope of eternal life.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you keep growing on the path of faith and receive more of God's grace and blessing. Amen.

v: having hope toward God, which these also themselves look for, that there will be a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust.
b: In our lives, time is very precious and brief. From the moment we are born, our journey through time begins, but we cannot know how long it will be. Like a movie of life, we can only keep going forward; we cannot start over or go back.

The road of life has many twists and challenges, and in the end everyone must face death. Even the greatest people must face death; it is a fixed fact that humanity cannot change. But in this passage we see a beautiful hope: the hope of resurrection.

For a Christian, death is not the final stop but the gate to eternal life. Because we know that by the power of God the dead, both the just and the unjust, will be raised. This is the hope of all Christians, and it is our hope for life. At the same time, the resurrection of Jesus Christ has opened the door of resurrection for us, so that we may find comfort and hope even in death.
We all know that life has many setbacks and difficulties, and may even meet death. But as Christians we have a solid hope, the hope of resurrection: that one day we will rise, just as Christ rose.

As we speak of this hope, I would like to share an inspiring story. There was a man named Nick who was born with disabilities in all four limbs. Yet despite his physical limitations, he did not give up his dreams and convictions. He studied hard and finally became a successful speaker and author.

Nick's success came partly from his effort and perseverance, and partly from his unwavering belief in Christ's resurrection. He believed that even though he suffered all kinds of hardship and setbacks in this world, in the end, by God's grace, he would receive new life and resurrection.

This story tells us that whatever difficulties and setbacks we face, if we have faith, we can overcome everything. For we have a mighty hope, and this hope comes from our faith in Christ's resurrection and is the promise we receive by God's grace.

Every challenge and difficulty we meet in life can make us feel despair, but when we have the hope of resurrection, we have the courage and strength to face them. For in Christ we receive not only eternal life, but also His grace and help in this life, so that we can walk steadily through every hard moment.

Finally, I want to bless each one of you, that in facing death and difficulty you may all have the hope of resurrection given by Christ Jesus. May we keep growing in His truth, and let this hope blossom and bear fruit in our lives.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you receive the hope of resurrection, and may you find strength and comfort in God's love and grace. Amen.

v: looking for the blessed hope and appearing of the glory of our great God and Savior, Jesus Christ,
b: On life's journey we inevitably meet all kinds of challenges and difficulties. But when we fix our eyes on heaven and wait for the blessed hope, we can steady our hearts and walk the rest of life's journey more firmly.

As Christians, the blessing we wait for does not come from outward material wealth or pleasure, but from the appearing of the glory of God and Jesus Christ. We are waiting for Jesus Christ to return and bring eternal redemption and glory. As the Bible says: “The righteous will live by his faith.” (Habakkuk 2:4)
While we wait, we must keep trusting and relying on God, like someone in a long tunnel waiting for the light to come.

A young girl had to give up her chance to go to university because of a sudden family crisis, and she felt very discouraged and despairing. But at that time she began to learn to rely on God and entrusted her life into His hands. In the end God gave her a new opportunity to start again in pursuing her dream, to finish her university studies, and to achieve remarkable success in her career.

This story tells us that when we face setbacks and difficulties in life, we should not give up hope and faith. Instead, we should hold tightly to hope and wait for God's guidance and blessing. As the Bible says: “Out of my distress, I called on Yah. Yah answered me with freedom.” (Psalm 118:5)
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. As you wait for the blessed hope, may you keep trusting and relying on God, may God's blessing always be with you, and may you show a heavenly and beautiful character on life's journey. Amen.

v: remembering without ceasing your work of faith and labor of love and perseverance of hope in our Lord Jesus Christ, before our God and Father.
b: This passage tells us that our faith as Christians is made up of faith, love and hope. These three are intertwined and affect one another, and they make our souls firm.

On our journey of faith we may meet all kinds of troubles and challenges, but if we hold on to hope and believe that Jesus Christ is our Redeemer, we can receive strength and courage to face everything. Like a ship sailing through a storm, only by looking at the bright lighthouse in the distance can it keep its course and reach its destination.

We can find inspiration in the story of Pastor Rick Warren. When his son Matthew died, he fell into deep grief. But in those sorrowful days he did not lose hope. By nurturing his faith and trust in God, he found the strength to face this challenge.

We can also find similar examples in our own lives. When we are about to face a difficulty or challenge, we can imagine ourselves as long-distance runners, with hope like the flag at the finish line. When we see that flag, we know that if we keep pressing forward, we will surely reach our destination. Hope is the wellspring of strength in our souls; it brings us endless energy and drive, so that we keep running in hardship and press ahead with courage.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. Because of the perseverance of hope in our Lord Jesus Christ, may you hold tightly to this light and hope on your journey of faith, trust God's grace and heart, treat all difficulties and challenges as nourishment for your faith, strengthen your faith, and experience God's presence and power. May you, because of hope, receive endless strength and wisdom in your work and labor, follow the Lord's will, and carry out His good plan. Amen.

t: The Hope Laid Up in Heaven
v: because of the hope which is laid up for you in the heavens, of which you heard before in the word of the truth of the Good News
b: Today let us talk about the hope laid up in heaven. Many things in life disappoint us and leave us discouraged, confused and let down. But we have a hope that goes beyond this world: the hope laid up in heaven. This hope does not come from our own strength or wisdom, but from the word of the truth of the Gospel that we believe.

There is a story about a young man's growth and hope. From childhood this young man lived in poverty, yet he was always full of faith and hope. He knew that although his parents could not give him a rich material life, they kept encouraging him to hold firmly to his faith and study hard. Under God's guidance, this young man was finally admitted to his ideal university, became an outstanding engineer, and achieved great success in his career.

This story tells us that by holding on to the hope of heaven we can overcome difficulties and pursue success. For we know that this world is not our eternal home; we have a better, richer home, our home in heaven.

The Bible tells us: “Our citizenship is in heaven, from where we also wait for a Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ.” (Philippians 3:20–21) In our home in heaven there is abundant peace, joy and contentment, and more importantly, eternal life, being with the Lord and enjoying blessing forever.

So let us encourage one another, strengthen our faith, and hold fast to the hope laid up in heaven, while working for the Lord in this world. Let us lay down every weight and burden and run toward that eternal home, pursuing the abundant life God gives.
In the Lord we can overcome difficulties and gain victory, because the Lord is with us; He is our help and our hope.
May we always keep faith, watch over one another, move forward together, and look forward to that wonderful homeland.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you stand firm on the road of pursuing the hope of heaven, full of joy and peace. Amen!

v: Therefore prepare your minds for action. Be sober, and set your hope fully on the grace that will be brought to you at the revelation of Jesus Christ—
b: Friends, this verse reminds us to keep our hearts disciplined at all times, to stay sober and self-controlled, and to look earnestly for the appearing of Jesus Christ, because the coming of this Savior will bring us great happiness and grace.

There is a very moving story about the transformation of a man with mental illness. This patient used to suffer frequent episodes, his emotions were extremely unstable, and he would even act violently at times. But when he heard the message about Jesus Christ, his life began to change. He began to look earnestly for Jesus' appearing, entrusting all his anxiety and worry to Him. Gradually this patient found inner calm and peace, and let God's love fill his heart.

Friends, although we may not have difficulties like this patient's, everyone faces some challenges and hardships. At such times let us also look earnestly for the appearing of Jesus Christ, open our hearts to Him, and let His love and grace fill our lives.

Let us also discipline our hearts, stay sober and self-controlled, not be swayed by the ways of the world, but wholeheartedly pursue God's will. Let us fix our focus on the appearing of Jesus Christ, because His coming brings us immeasurable joy, peace and love.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you all discipline your hearts and look earnestly for the appearing of Jesus Christ, and let God's grace become the most beautiful part of your lives. Amen!

t: Hoping for a New Heaven and Earth
v: But, according to his promise, we look for new heavens and a new earth, in which righteousness dwells.
b: This verse helps us remember that this world is not forever. Even if we face difficulty, setback, disappointment, or even death, we can hope for the coming of the new heaven and new earth. This new heaven and earth will be a place full of righteousness, where we can be with God forever.

There is a story about a man who lost everything in a great fire, including his family and his property. He felt desperate and heartbroken, and did not know how to go on living. But he was fortunate to meet another person who had gone through something similar. That person told him that even if he had lost everything, he should not lose hope, because better things were waiting for him in the future. He could start again, build a new home, meet a new family, and have new wealth. After hearing these words, the man found his faith again and began rebuilding his life.

This story tells us that even in the darkest times we must not lose hope and faith. For God has promised us that in the new heaven and earth righteousness will dwell. As 1 Peter 1:3 says: “He has become our father again, begotten us through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead into a living hope.” We can believe that because of Christ's resurrection, we too will have new life and new hope.

Let us not give up, but keep working and moving forward, because one day we will enter that new heaven and earth full of righteousness. Let us remember what 1 Corinthians 2:9 says: “What things an eye didn’t see, and an ear didn’t hear, which didn’t enter into the heart of man, these God has prepared for those who love him.”
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you keep hope and faith in the face of difficulty, believing that in the new heaven and earth righteousness dwells. Amen!

v: who through him are believers in God, who raised him from the dead and gave him glory, so that your faith and hope might be in God.
b: In this world we meet all kinds of difficulties, and sometimes we may feel helpless, lonely or lost. But this verse tells us that because we trust the God who raised Christ from the dead, our faith and hope are in God.

Let us look at a story to illustrate this truth. A young man felt utterly hopeless because of the pressures of life, and had even thought of ending his life. One day, walking in a park, he saw a little sapling trying to break through the gray concrete to grow into a big tree. The young man was moved by the sapling's perseverance and resilience, and began to understand that hope is in God, and that God is truly a great and faithful Creator. As this verse says, let our faith and hope be in God.

In the face of the difficulties and challenges of life, we always feel confused and helpless. But when we believe in Jesus Christ, who rose from the dead, and take Him as our Savior, we will find that God is with us and that God will help us through every difficulty.
So let us not lose hope and faith. Let us believe in this great and faithful God, who guides us through every step of life.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you go on believing, stand firm and be full of hope on your journey through life, because God is surely with you. Amen!

v: The prospect of the righteous is joy, but the hope of the wicked will perish.
b: This reminds me of an old story. A farmer sowed seed in his field. He worked hard plowing, watering and weeding, but when harvest time came, he gathered only a single bean vine. He was very disappointed, because he had put in so much effort and received such a trivial reward.

But the farmer never gave up; he kept working and living diligently. As time passed, when he went back to the field, he found that his hard work had borne a rich harvest. His field was covered with beautiful flowers and fruit. From this story the farmer learned an important lesson: hope and patience are the key to success. Just as he had to wait for his field to produce a harvest, we must cultivate and keep the right attitude, and keep striving toward our goals without slackening, even when we meet challenges and failure.

The righteous person in this verse refers to one who practices justice, follows God's will, and keeps working at tending his own life. Such a person has a beautiful hope, because they know that what they pursue is right, and they believe their pursuit has meaning. When we act before God and pursue righteousness, we are like that farmer: we must wait patiently for God's grace and blessing.

In contrast, the expectation of the wicked leads them to destruction. They have no right goal or direction; they pursue violence, wealth or power while ignoring morality and conscience, and in the end they will surely face God's judgment and rebuke.

So let us become righteous people, follow God's will, and keep pressing forward with a beautiful hope and firm faith, never giving up even in adversity. May our lives be filled with more joy and hope because of our faith, for we believe God is an almighty heavenly Father who will surely watch over us and give us His blessing and mercy.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you stand firm on the path of holiness, keep on cultivating, and wait with faith and hope for God's blessing and grace. May you become a righteous person, and through faith receive joy and peace. Amen!

v: But I will always hope, and will add to all of your praise.
b: In life we often meet difficulties and setbacks that easily make us lose our direction and drive. But the psalmist tells us that hope is a key resource that can help us keep the right direction and a firm perseverance.

We can learn the spirit of hope from others, such as a young man named Patrick Henry Hughes. Hughes was born with disabilities; he could not walk and could not see. Even so, he learned to play the violin and performed in his university marching band. Even more amazing, Hughes' father became his eyes and legs, pushing him to classes and rehearsals every day. This perseverance and hope touched the whole community and inspired many people.

This also tells us that in hard times hope is our best support. When we face difficulties, we should not give up, but actively look for solutions and believe that God will help us when we need Him most.

Let us follow in the psalmist's steps: always hope, and praise God all the more. As Christians, we believe that God will uphold us and give us strength to overcome any difficulty. Let us lay down our worries, hold on to hope, and trust that God can help us through each day of life.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you find true strength and direction in hope. Amen!

v: Remember your word to your servant, because you gave me hope.
b: In life we always meet setbacks and disappointments, as if we had lost our direction and hope. But when we have God's word as our guide and support, we can find the drive to pick ourselves up and go forward again.
It is like a mountain climber who meets an accident on the climb and loses his way. If he has an accurate map and a guide who knows the route, he can find his direction and confidence again.

In the same way, on the climb of life we also meet all kinds of challenges and difficulties, but we can trust that God's word is our best guide and help, so that we may have hope and find our direction again.

In the Bible we can find many promises and much guidance, such as Psalm 23: “Yahweh is my shepherd: I shall lack nothing. He makes me lie down in green pastures. He leads me beside still waters. He restores my soul. He guides me in the paths of righteousness for his name’s sake.” This lets us know that in hard times God is our shepherd and guide. God knows our needs and knows our future, so let us put our faith and hope in God's hands, trusting that He will lead us toward a bright future.

A story tells us about the power of hope. Long ago, a sailor was shipwrecked by a storm and stranded on a small island, with no food or water and no way to escape. But he did not give up his hope; he believed God would rescue him. While waiting for rescue he noticed that there were many bird eggs on the island. He began gathering them and, using the sun, worked out a way to hatch them, and in the end he succeeded in getting enough food and water, and was finally rescued.
This story tells us that even in the most desperate moments, as long as we keep hope and faith, we can find ways and strength to solve our problems.

So let us remember God's word, trust His promises, and keep faith and hope. As Psalm 121:1–2 says: “I will lift up my eyes to the hills. Where does my help come from? My help comes from Yahweh, who made heaven and earth.” Let us believe that whatever difficulties we face, God is our help and deliverer.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you keep faith and hope in difficulty, and trust in God's guidance and promises. Amen!

t: Hoping for What We Cannot See
v: But if we hope for that which we don’t see, we wait for it with patience.
b: In life there are many times when we are waiting for something: waiting for a child to be born, waiting for a new job, waiting for a cure. Whenever the time drags on, we feel anxious and discouraged, because we cannot see the outcome we hope for. Yet this is also when we must learn to wait patiently.

I once heard a story about a man waiting for rain in the desert. He planted some plants in the desert, but only when the rain came would he see the fruit of the harvest. This man had great faith; he believed that waiting was worth it. He kept watering and tending the plants, and even though he could not see results, he still believed that the day the rain would come.

In the same way, when we wait in life, we also need to believe and persevere. We must wait patiently and keep working and giving, not giving up even if we cannot see results. For if we have hope, we can endure and wait, and trust that the result will surely come.

This is also what the Bible teaches, as 1 Corinthians 15:58 says: “Therefore, my beloved brothers, be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the Lord’s work, knowing that your labor is not in vain in the Lord.” We must always abound in the Lord's work, steadfast and immovable, in order to keep our faith.

While we wait, let us not look only at the difficulties and challenges before us, but lift our eyes to the hope we cannot see. In the waiting we need to walk with God and receive strength and comfort through prayer. This too is the way of faith, hope and love that we must learn.
pr: God, in the process of waiting, may we have firm faith, patient waiting, and courage that does not give up. The Lord Jesus also said: “All things whatever you pray and ask for, believe that you have received them, and you shall have them.” (Mark 11:24) Let us believe, pray and wait, and when the moment comes, let us boldly declare: “I waited, and now I see my hope.”
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you receive the strength of faith, hope and love as you wait. May you keep learning to wait patiently and trust that the hope you cannot see will surely come. Amen!

v: For whatever things were written before were written for our learning, that through perseverance and through encouragement of the Scriptures we might have hope.
b: This verse reminds us of the importance of Scripture, from which we learn how to live, how to endure, and how to receive hope. In our own lives we often need this kind of help and guidance.

I remember a woman who said, “I once met a very great difficulty, but when I began to read the Bible, I found that many people in it had faced similar problems and found solutions in Scripture.” This story tells us how important it is to find guidance for life and ways to solve our problems in the Bible.

Moreover, in this world full of challenges and uncertainty, we also need hope. A young man once said, “When I lost my job, I felt despair and helplessness. But when I read the Bible, I found that God's word is full of hope, and I began to believe that God would bring me a better future.” This too reminds us that when we face difficulties and setbacks, the hope in Scripture can give us strength and courage.
pr: May we find in Scripture guidance for life, ways to solve problems, and the power of hope, so that in this world full of challenges we may stand firm in our faith and keep walking in God's way.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you receive hope through the patience and encouragement of the Scriptures. Amen!

v: Now may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that you may abound in hope in the power of the Holy Spirit.
b: In this age full of challenges and change, we all need hope. People who have gone through setbacks, failure, illness, or even the loss of a loved one may fall into despair and powerlessness. But God's word tells us that He fills our hearts with all joy and peace, and through God's great power and the help of the Holy Spirit we find hope again.

We can understand the importance of hope from an example in everyday life. There was an American baseball player named George Denton who went through many setbacks and losses, but he still kept hope, because he believed he could become an outstanding player. In the end he became a star of professional baseball, because even in difficulty he still believed in himself and in God's leading.

In the same way, we too can have hope, because we trust God's leading and power, and believe He will open a road for us so that we can overcome any difficulty and challenge. Let us remember: “Rejoice in the Lord always! Again I will say, Rejoice!” (Philippians 4:4)
So let us keep our faith, firmly believe God's word, and live in hope. In this way our lives will be full of joy and peace, and because we are filled with the Holy Spirit, we will abound in hope.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May the Lord's hope overflow in your life. Amen!

v: bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, and endures all things.
b: In our lives we sometimes meet setbacks and losses, and even feel confused and in despair, but the Bible tells us to hope all things, keeping faith and hope in the midst of difficulty. This reminds me of a story.

There was a professional soccer player who, in his youth, suffered from severe arthritis that kept him from playing. He once told people, “I have lost my life, because soccer was everything to me.” But he did not give up completely. He kept working hard at his rehabilitation and kept hoping to return to the field. Finally, after a long period of hard training, he returned to the soccer field and became a successful professional player. This player tells us that when we meet difficulty we should not give up hope and faith, because God's grace and power can help us overcome everything.

“Hope all things” does not mean that we should cling to fantasies, but that while waiting for God's promises to be fulfilled, we should keep firm faith and hope. Hope is a positive attitude; it keeps our hearts open, lets us accept the challenges and opportunities of life, and turns anxiety and fear into courage and strength.

In our lives, unexpected things sometimes happen that make us feel there is no hope for life. But the Bible tells us to believe God in all things, because He is a faithful and loving God who will not leave us alone and helpless. When we entrust our lives to God, He gives us strength and wisdom to help us overcome all difficulties and challenges.

In this world full of challenges and change, the Bible tells us to endure all things. This means that we need to keep patience and steadfastness in life, so that even when we meet difficulty and devastation, we can keep faith and hope. It is like a strong tree that twists and sways in wind and rain, yet stands firm in order to take in sunlight and water and grow strong. As the Bible promises: “Be faithful until death, and I will give you the crown of life.” (Revelation 2:10)
Let us keep an attitude of hoping, believing and enduring in life, trusting God's love and grace and the wonderful future He has prepared for us.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you keep firm faith and hope in life, gain victory out of difficulty, and bring glory to God's name. Amen!

v: Our hope for you is steadfast, knowing that, since you are partakers of the sufferings, so you are also of the comfort.
b: In this passage Paul tells the church in Corinth that even in suffering we can still hold hope, because we know we are not alone but walk together with other believers. In this world we inevitably meet difficulties and setbacks, but in those moments we can rely on God's promises and the power of the Holy Spirit to stand up.

An inspiring story tells us that when we face challenges and misfortune, hope can truly change everything. A young man was diagnosed with a rare disease, and the doctors told him he had only one year to live. But he did not give up; he decided to use the time he had left to do something meaningful. He took an active part in charity work, helped people in need, and wrote a book to encourage and inspire others. Finally, two years later, the doctors found that his illness had miraculously disappeared. This young man's story tells us that even in unpredictable circumstances, as long as we have hope and faith, wonderful change can come.

As this verse says, our hope is steadfast, because we know we are not alone. When we walk with other believers and share each other's difficulties and setbacks, we can support and encourage one another, and keep watch and pray together. Such mutual love and help makes us firmer and gives us more hope as we face the challenges and difficulties of the future.

So let us keep looking in Scripture for promises and comfort, and hold tightly to the steadfast hope we have, for this is a strength we can rely on in facing the challenges of life. Let us love one another and support one another, go forward together, and jointly witness God's great power and wonderful works.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you hold hope at every moment of life, and on your journey of faith support one another and pursue God's will and plan together. Amen!

v: to the end that we should be to the praise of his glory, we who had before hoped in Christ.
b: This passage tells us that as Christians we have hope in Christ. What is this hope? It is that one day we will enter heaven and be with God forever in Christ. When we have this hope, even in present suffering we can be full of faith and peace.

How, then, can we keep hope in suffering? I would like to share a story with you. A young girl fell seriously ill and lost both legs and her right hand. When she woke up, she was very depressed and did not know how to go on living. But her mother told her, “You still have one hand, and you can do many things with it. If you still have such faith and hope, you will be able to get through this challenge and become a better, stronger person.”

With her mother's encouragement, the girl began to rebuild her life. She learned to use a prosthesis, learned to drive and to live independently. She worked hard to overcome setbacks, became a successful professional woman, and even founded an organization to help others with physical disabilities.

This story tells us that even in the darkest times, keeping faith and hope is very important. We can gain such strength and courage through prayer and our relationship with God. When we believe God's promises and seek His leading in daily life, we can overcome challenges just like that girl and become stronger and more successful people.

So let us keep in mind what this passage says: those who hope in Christ bring praise to His glory. When we go through suffering and setbacks, let us turn our eyes toward heaven, rely on our faith and hope, and keep pressing forward with courage. May the Lord give us strength and help us live out our identity as Christians.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you enjoy an abundant life in faith, hope and love. Amen!

v: according to my earnest expectation and hope, that I will in no way be disappointed, but with all boldness, as always, now also Christ will be magnified in my body, whether by life or by death.
b: This passage tells us that as long as we follow God's will and pursue what we earnestly long for and hope for, we will not be ashamed. Boldly pursuing our dreams is the way that Christ can be magnified in us as always.

A young man named Peter loved singing from childhood, but his parents wanted him to study for a more stable career and become an accountant or lawyer. This choice troubled Peter greatly, because what he truly loved deep in his heart was music. But he still followed his parents' wishes and began his road of accounting studies. But once he started working, he found that his heart was not truly fulfilled, and he felt that he could not keep going on this road.

One day Peter decided to be bold and try joining a singing contest, and he felt his soul set free. Although Peter met setbacks, he did not give up, and kept pursuing his true dream. In the end he became an outstanding singer, bringing his music and beautiful emotion to many more people.

This story tells us that as long as we follow our hearts and pursue what we truly love, we can live out our true selves. At the same time, when we boldly pursue our dreams, Christ will also be magnified in us as always, giving us strength and courage. So we need not fear failure or setbacks; we need only believe in ourselves, trust God's leading, and walk steadily toward our goals.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for opening the door of courage and hope for us. May we, on life's road, press forward according to our dreams and Your will. Give us firm courage, so that we boldly pursue the dreams we love and dedicate our talents and love to You.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May God's grace be with you. Amen!

v: to whom God was pleased to make known what are the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles, which is Christ in you, the hope of glory.
b: On life's journey we often meet setbacks and difficulties that leave us discouraged and in despair. But when we believe in Jesus Christ, who has become in our hearts the hope of glory, we can see the beauty and worth in life.

There was a young man who had once been a very successful entrepreneur, but because of a failed investment he lost all his property and reputation, and fell into a desperate situation. At first he felt utterly hopeless and at his wits' end, but he decided to believe God's word, the very verse we are quoting today. He believed that Christ in him was the hope of glory, and he began to rebuild his life.

This young man devoted all his time and energy to the work of helping others. He organized a charity that helped people who had lost their homes find hope for living again. His work gave him back his own sense of worth and purpose, and many people benefited from his love and generosity.

Each of us can have this kind of hope, believing even in the hardest moments that Christ in us is the hope of glory. When we focus on helping others, we discover our own worth and purpose, and we can feel the rich glory that comes from God.
So let us believe together that Christ in us is the hope of glory, and be willing to use our own strength to help others, so that they too can find hope and worth for their lives.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May God's rich glory always be with you. Amen!

v: For what is our hope, or joy, or crown of rejoicing? Isn’t it even you, before our Lord Jesus at his coming?
b: When we think about the meaning and direction of life, we often feel confused and lost. But there is a hope and joy we can rely on: the return of our Lord Jesus. When we stand before Jesus, we will no longer have any questions. This hope gives us firm faith and makes us live out the Christian life more sincerely.

Let us think: if everything in life went smoothly, would we still need such a mighty hope? But the facts are often not like that. When we face difficulties and challenges, hope gives us strength and courage to overcome them. Like a sailor in a fierce storm at sea, who can keep going only by trusting in his destination, our hope is the compass on life's road, guiding us to press forward with courage.

Let us return to the crown mentioned in this verse. It refers to the reward Christians will receive in heaven. This crown is not obtained through our own merit, but through the redemption and grace of the Lord Jesus. We need only fix our eyes on Him, trust Him, and obey His will, and we can receive this crown.

Let us remember that the Christian's hope is built on the return of Jesus Christ. In this uncertain and unstable world, this hope can bring us calm and comfort. We can be confident that in the love and grace of our Lord Jesus Christ we will be able to bear all hardship and adversity.

Let us also realize that, as Christians, we must share this hope with others, so that they too can experience this wonderful hope. We can inspire them through the testimony of our own lives, so that they too understand the hope and joy found in Christ.
pr: Lord, let us keep growing in faith, hope and love, and share this hope with those who need it. “
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you” — may we be those who pass on hope and love in this world. “Amen!”

v: Now our Lord Jesus Christ himself, and God our Father, who loved us and gave us eternal comfort and good hope through grace,
b: This passage speaks of a good hope. What, then, is a good hope? For different people a good hope may mean different things, but from the Bible we can find an answer we all share.

Many times, when we face difficulties and challenges, we lose hope and feel despair and helplessness. But this passage tells us that in God we can have a good hope. This is because our Lord Jesus Christ loves us and graciously gives us eternal comfort and good hope.

In this world we will go through many setbacks and failures, but when we believe in God's love and grace, we can stand courageously in difficulty and also look forward to a good hope for the future. There was a young girl whose parents divorced, and her family fell on hard times; she felt lost and in despair. But she began to believe in God and entrusted her life to Him, and with the support of her faith she found a new purpose and meaning in life, and began to show strength for continual growth and advance. She believed that even when she did not reach out for help, God would prepare a smooth road for her and give her a good hope.

In the same way, when we face hard times in our own lives, we can also believe in God's love and grace and trust that He will give us a good hope. Let us learn to trust God and believe that He will prepare a wonderful future for us.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May a good hope always accompany you, give you firm faith and hope, and let you always feel God's love and grace. Amen!

v: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who according to his great mercy caused us to be born again to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,
b: We all long to have hope, because hope can sustain us in facing the challenges and difficulties of life. The “living hope” here fills us with confidence and expectation for the future. What is this living hope? It is the hope found in Christ. Christ's rising from the dead proved that He is the Son of God and our Redeemer, and now He sits at the right hand of the Father, interceding for us. Because of this living hope, we can have courage and strength to face everything.

A man named Mr. Helang received a call from the military during his son's military service, telling him that his son had been killed in action. But a few days later he received another call, telling him it was only a mistake and that his son was actually alive. The father went through extreme grief and loss, but when he learned that his son was alive, a living hope arose in his heart, and he was filled with confidence and expectation for the future.

In the same way, Christ's resurrection brings a living hope, so that we do not lose courage and faith in difficulties and trials. We can trust God's promises and know that He will surely accomplish His good plan. As the Bible says: “For I know the thoughts that I think toward you,” says Yahweh, “thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you hope and a future.” (Jeremiah 29:11)

Let us keep reminding ourselves that Christ's resurrection brings a living hope that fills us with faith and expectation on life's journey. Even in the face of adversity and challenge, we can rely on His strength and grace and go on steadfastly. Psalm 27:13 tells us: “I am still confident of this: I will see the goodness of Yahweh in the land of the living.”

In today's message we learned that Christ's resurrection brings a living hope that fills us with faith and courage on life's journey. Let us rely on His grace and strength, and go on steadfastly without giving up.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you keep a living hope at all times, and under God's leading receive His shelter and protection in every stage of life. Amen!

v: But since we belong to the day, let’s be sober, putting on the breastplate of faith and love, and for a helmet, the hope of salvation.
b: In this passage Paul tells the believers that as Christians we must be sober at all times and put on the armor of faith, love and hope. Imagine a soldier on the battlefield without a helmet: he would hardly survive the enemy's attack. In the same way, if we do not put on the helmet of hope on the spiritual battlefield, it will be hard to win against Satan's temptations and trials.

But what is hope? Hope is expectation and confidence for the future; it is trusting God and believing His promises. In life we sometimes experience loss, defeat and disappointment, and these negative feelings may make us give up hope for the future. Yet Paul reminds us to put on the helmet of hope, because only those who have hope can persevere through hardship and keep moving forward.

There was a young girl named Emily who suffered from a rare disease, and the doctors told her she had only a few months to live. Yet she still faced each day with hope and faith, believing that God would release her body from its pain and bring her eternal hope. After Emily finished her journey in life, she left a letter in which she wrote: “When I leave this world, I leave with no regrets, because I know I am about to be reunited with my Lord.” Emily kept hope even in the most desperate circumstances, and this shows us what true faith and hope are.

In our lives we may sometimes meet loss, defeat and disappointment, but as long as we keep trusting God and believing His promises, we can put on the helmet of hope, press ahead with courage, and face each day full of faith and hope. Let us keep on walking steadfastly on the spiritual battlefield, putting on the armor of faith, love and hope, overcoming Satan's trials and temptations, and moving toward the heavenly promise.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May your heart be full of faith, hope and love, may you not give up easily, and may you follow God's will without wavering. Amen!

v: But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts. Always be ready to give an answer to everyone who asks you a reason concerning the hope that is in you, with humility and fear,
b: Hope is the core of faith, the firmest conviction in our hearts. And this core of faith comes from hearts that honor Christ the Lord as holy. When we put God in the highest place in our hearts, we become like a tree of hope, drawing nourishment from deep in the roots and growing strong, with firm faith and eternal hope.

When people ask us the reason for the hope in our hearts, we must be ready to answer. We can use our own experiences and testimony, or illustrations from life, to explain the hope that comes from honoring Christ as holy. For example, putting God in the highest place in our hearts is like seeing the first ray of sunlight at dawn, leading us into a new day, which is that eternal hope.

But when we answer people's questions, we must answer with gentleness and reverence. It is like leading a blind person across the road: we need careful guidance and considerate care, so that the person can cross safely. In the same way, when we answer questions, we need to speak with others in a considerate and caring spirit, sharing the hope we have in an atmosphere of calm and love.

Let us make a heart that honors Christ as holy the foundation of our faith, and answer people's questions about the reason for hope with gentleness and reverence, so that the world may be brighter and better because of us.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you have firm faith and eternal hope in Christ. Amen!

v: Therefore, beloved, seeing that you look for these things, be diligent to be found in peace, without defect and blameless in his sight.
b: While we look forward to Christ's return, we must also be diligent, paying attention to our lives and keeping our distance from the stains of the world, living simply and blamelessly, so that we may meet the Lord in peace.

On life's journey we sometimes meet hardship and setbacks, and may even feel despair and loss. But God's word reminds us to hope, and also to be diligent. It is like a traveler on a long road who hopes for the final destination but must stay alert at all times and watch for dangers on the way so as not to be hurt. In the same way, on life's journey we must hope for the future and pursue the truth, but at the same time be diligent, keeping our lives pure and upright.

A girl loved gymnastics and dreamed of winning the championship. She practiced gymnastics at home every day. But one day she accidentally sprained her ankle, and the doctor told her she had to rest for a month and could not practice. The girl was disappointed and discouraged, and felt she could no longer hope to become a gymnastics champion. But her coach told her that as long as she kept a good attitude and good habits, her injury would heal quickly. The girl listened to her coach, carefully used the therapy equipment, and paid attention to her diet and rest, and in the end her injury soon healed. This story tells us that even in difficulty and setback, as long as we are diligent and keep the right attitude and conduct, we can overcome difficulty and reach our goals.

So let us join the Bible in its call: “Seeing that you look for these things, be diligent to be found in peace, without defect and blameless in his sight.” Hope is a positive power that gives us faith, hope and love, and lets us walk steadfastly into the future. In this world full of challenges and change, let us be like the girl, keeping a good attitude and good habits, and diligently pursuing truth and righteousness.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you be full of faith, hope and love on life's journey, and walk steadfastly toward the future. Amen!

v: and perseverance, proven character; and proven character, hope;
b: There are always all kinds of challenges in life, and in these challenges and adversities we need to learn patience and seasoned maturity. Patience is not just waiting; it is moving forward while waiting. Maturity is not age; it is experience and wisdom.

We see many seasoned people in the Bible, such as Peter, the disciple of Jesus, who even in old age proclaimed the gospel without wavering, and did not shrink back even at the moment of his martyrdom. There was also Moses, who led the Israelites in the barren wilderness. Facing the plight of having no water and no food, he cried out to God, and God gave a wonderful grace so that the Israelites could survive and prosper.

In our own lives we also meet all kinds of challenges and difficulties, but when we learn endurance and patience, we can become more seasoned and wise, and this will help us face future challenges and difficulties better. And as we mature, our hope also comes forth. For we know that God is faithful and He will be with us; whatever valleys we pass through or storms we go through, we can trust His lovingkindness and provision.

We can also learn from the Israelites in the wilderness to cry out to God in hardship and rely on His faithfulness and grace. When we do this, God will surely do wonderful and beautiful things in our lives, and He will lead us toward a brighter tomorrow. So let us learn endurance, patience and maturity in life, and meet each new challenge full of faith and hope.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you have enough patience and wisdom in life to become more mature and seasoned, keep hope and faith in hardship, and trust that God's promises will surely be fulfilled in your life. Amen!

v: and hope doesn’t disappoint us, because God’s love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit who was given to us.
b: I believe we have all experienced loss and despair, and at such times what we need is hope. Yet when we lose hope, there is one thing we must not do, and that is feel shame. When hope is lost, a sense of loss and self-blame may arise in our hearts, but this is not what God wants to tell us. On the contrary, He wants us to know that hope does not put us to shame, because He has given the Holy Spirit in our hearts, so that God's love is poured out within us.

There was a man who lived in extreme poverty and hardship; he had lost everything and felt despair and loneliness. Yet he did not give up hope, and kept believing in God's love and His plan. In the end, through an unexpected opportunity, he got a good job and a healthy family. This man tells us that even in the hardest times hope is still there, and as long as we believe and let God's Holy Spirit be poured out within us, we can see a beautiful future.

In our lives we may sometimes meet setbacks and failures, but this does not mean we should not pursue hope. On the contrary, we should hold tightly to the hope God has given and to His promise to pour His love into our hearts.
Let us thank God, because of the Holy Spirit and love He has given, we can face the challenges and difficulties of life full of faith, hope and love.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you hold on to hope at every moment, trust God's plan, and be filled with His love. Amen!

v: but Christ is faithful as a Son over his house. We are his house, if we hold fast our confidence and the glorying of our hope firm to the end.
b: This verse reminds us that Christ is our head, and we must rely on His guidance and direction to build the house of God. It also means that when we trust in Christ, He leads us to a place full of hope, giving us courage to keep going.

I have experienced this hope and courage. Some time ago I was going through a very hard stage of life. I felt despair and loneliness and could see no way out. But I still prayed and kept seeking Christ's guidance and will. In the end Christ led me to find a way to solve my problem. At that time I deeply realized that as long as we hold on to hope and faith, we can reach the goal God has given us.

At the same time, this verse reminds us to have a hope to glory in and courage, which requires us to keep faith and patience throughout our lives and face difficulties and challenges bravely. Like a famous long-distance runner who once said, “I will not give up, because I know victory is waiting for me far ahead.”

So when we meet adversity, let us keep in mind the truth presented in this passage, and believe that Christ can lead us out of our trouble and build a firmer house of God. At the same time, let us encourage ourselves and those around us to face the challenges of life bravely, holding fast to a hope to glory in and to courage. Wherever we are, as long as we trust Christ's guidance and protection, we can gain success and victory.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for giving us this precious journey of faith, and for giving us courage and hope to face the many challenges of life. Please keep leading us on the right path, and give us a hope to glory in and courage, so that we can walk steadfastly to the end.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you all. May you receive strength in Christ and experience the fullness of God. Amen!

v: if it is so that you continue in the faith, grounded and steadfast, and not moved away from the hope of the Good News which you heard, which was proclaimed in all creation under heaven, of which I, Paul, was made a servant.
b: The gospel is the most precious food in our lives, and it carries us through the deserts and sufferings of life. Yet in the face of adversity and challenge, we may lose hope and even become disheartened about the gospel. But this is not God's plan for us.

Imagine that you are walking along a road and suddenly come to a river you do not know how to get around. How would you feel? Some people might feel despair and confusion, but the Bible records that Joshua, the leader of Israel, believed God's promise and led the Israelites across the Jordan River when its waters were at their highest (Joshua 3:14–17). This is the power of hope! Hope lets us trust God's plan and promises, and even in hard times we can keep moving forward.

A story tells of a young man who came down from the mountain and saw an old man chopping down a tree. He asked the old man, “Why don’t you use a chainsaw? It would be much faster.” The old man answered, “I only have an axe. If I used a chainsaw, my body would become lazy and lose the ability to use hand tools.” This is a good illustration, telling us that when we face difficulty and challenge, we should not give up easily, nor depend too much on the convenience of modern technology, but overcome adversity through firm faith and lasting effort.

Let us keep trusting God and not lose the hope of the gospel. For the God we believe in is eternal, His love does not change, and His promises are dependable. As the Bible says: “Yes, no one who waits for you will be disappointed.” (Psalm 25:3)
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you stand firm on the path of faith, let hope fill your heart, and let God's love and promises be the drive that moves you forward. Amen!

v: He who doesn’t love doesn’t know God, for God is love.
b: In this world full of conflict, war, disaster and pain, we often feel despair and helplessness. But let us not forget that God is the very essence of love, and this is the core of our faith. Love is God's character, and also the expression of His grace and lovingkindness to us. Whenever we face difficulty and challenge, as long as we hold tightly to God's love, we can receive strength and comfort.

A story tells how a mother used love to help her child stand up again. This child was bullied by classmates at school and became depressed and withdrawn, and no longer wanted to go to school. The mother sensed her child's pain, and every day she spent time talking with him, praising the good things he did at the right moments, and telling him how loved and treasured he was. Through his mother's love and care, the child gradually regained his confidence and stood up again to face his challenges.

Just as this mother used the power of love to care for and encourage her child, God also uses His love to care for and encourage us. When we feel fragile and helpless, let us remember these words: “God is love.” He keeps showing us His love and compassion, telling us how much He cares about us. In trust and faith we can live out a life of love, and let God's love be shown in our lives.
Let us pray to God together, asking Him to give us more love, so that we can show His love and grace in this world.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you find strength and comfort in God's love, may you live out a life of love, and become a witness to God's love. Amen!

v: In this is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us, and sent his Son as the atoning sacrifice for our sins.
b: These words are magnificent, and make us realize that love is not only a feeling but also an action.

In life there are many people and situations that need us to sacrifice our time, money or other things to help them. This requires us to have great love and the support of faith. If we have no love, we cannot truly know God, because God Himself is love.
Recently I heard a story about love. It tells us that even in the most difficult circumstances, love brings miracles.

The story is about a mother and her son who had a car accident in a snow-covered mountain region, and the car slid off a cliff. The mother was badly injured in the car, while the son was trapped in the snow. Then a sledder came by and told the mother that he could take her down the mountain, but he could not save her son, because the sled could bear the weight of only one person. The mother watched her son shivering in the snow, crying helplessly.
At that moment the mother made a moving decision: she chose to stay and let the sledder take her son first. In the end the mother died from severe hypothermia, but her son was saved.

This story tells us that love can go beyond everything. The mother's love and spirit of sacrifice brought her son's rescue and new life. In the same way, in our lives there are many opportunities to sacrifice ourselves, but if we have the support of strong faith and a heart full of love, even in the hardest situations we can receive God's help and the best outcome.

So let us be filled with God's love every day, love others, sacrifice ourselves, and serve others as Jesus Christ did, and keep in mind: “Above all things be earnest in your love among yourselves, for love covers a multitude of sins.” (1 Peter 4:8)
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you find true freedom and joy in love, and be a witness to love in your life, bringing others faith, hope and love. Amen!

v: But God commends his own love toward us, in that while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.
b: When we think about God's love, we find that it is beyond understanding and beyond measure. For the love God shows us is based on His own nature, not on our behavior or character. The reason God loves us is that He Himself is love.

In today's world we are often told that we can receive others' love and approval only when we show enough worth. But God's standard of love is different. While we were still sinners, Christ died for us. This means that we do not need to do anything, and God already loves us. How overwhelming that is!

I would like to share a story to show how important God's love is to us. A boy was bullied by classmates at school, and felt very desperate and lonely. But he tried going to church and began to learn about God's love. He learned that God's love is unconditional and can be enjoyed without his doing anything. This made him feel accepted and loved, and changed how he saw himself and others.

In the same way, in our lives many challenges and difficulties often arise. But Christ died for us while we were still sinners, making God's love plain, which shows that God is willing to pay everything to save us. This is a very encouraging fact, especially when we are in trouble and doubt.

Let us remember what Romans 5:8 says: “But God commends his own love toward us, in that while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.” God's love is beyond compare, but it can give us comfort, strength and hope. Let us treasure this love and pass it on, so that more people can experience God's grace and lovingkindness.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May God's love, grace and peace always be with you. Amen!

v: This is love, that we should walk according to his commandments. This is the commandment, even as you heard from the beginning, that you should walk in it.
b: What is true love? In this world many people define love as strong feeling or romantic emotion, but God sees love differently from us. He asks us to love one another, which is a choice in action, not merely a promise in words. When we act according to the Lord's commandments, we show His love for us.

A young man once asked an elder about love. “Please tell me, what is true love?” The elder thought for a moment, then picked up a large stone, put it in the young man's hand, and said, “Go to the top of that mountain and give this stone to a passerby, telling him it is a gift from you.”

The young man followed the elder's instructions, climbed to the top of the mountain, found a passerby, and handed him the stone. When he told the passerby it was a gift, the passerby frowned and said, “It’s just a stone.”

The young man went back to the elder, who asked him what had happened. The young man replied that he had told the passerby it was a gift from him, but the passerby did not think it was a valuable gift.
The elder smiled and said to the young man, “Now take this stone and climb to the top of the mountain again, but this time you must let the passerby know the value of this stone.”

Following the elder's instructions, the young man climbed the mountain again and met another passerby. When he handed over the stone, he explained where it came from and its value. The passerby smiled and accepted the stone with great gratitude, because he knew that behind this meaningful gift lay a special value.

In the same way, when we love one another, not only with promises in words but with a choice in action, we can show Jesus' love for us. When, like that young man, we convey to others the value we have received in Christ, we can make others feel God's love and grace. Let us act according to the Lord's commandments every day and love one another. This is true love.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May God's love always surround you, and may His grace and peace be with you at every step you take. Amen!

v: One who has my commandments and keeps them, that person is one who loves me. One who loves me will be loved by my Father, and I will love him, and will reveal myself to him.”
b: This verse tells us that if we truly love the Lord Jesus, we will keep the commandments He has given. If we do not obey the Lord's word, we cannot show our love for Him. On the other hand, if we obey His word and let it be the guide of our lives, then we can truly show our love for Him.

Let us think: what would happen if we truly loved God and kept His commandments? In fact, when we truly obey God's will, His rich blessing and grace fill our lives. This is not only a spiritual benefit, but also one in our daily lives and work. From my own experience, when we act according to God's guidance, we can better reach our goals, and our lives become more peaceful and meaningful.

There is an inspiring story I would like to share with you. There was a young man who worked hard but always felt he lacked direction and purpose. He began to look for spiritual guidance, reading the Bible and praying every day, longing to know God's will. Slowly he began to find his life becoming fuller. He began to understand his true purpose, and began to find greater success in his work and relationships. Most important, he began to feel God's love and grace, which poured endless hope and strength into his life.

Let us also learn, like this young man, to obey the commandments in the Bible and apply them in our daily lives. When we truly love the Lord Jesus and act according to His word, we can experience God's rich blessing and grace, and bear spiritual fruit in this world.

Let us pray to God together, asking Him to help us keep His commandments every day and receive His abundant blessing and grace. May our lives be full of God's love and His Holy Spirit, so that we may be true believers, acting steadfastly according to His will, and become His light and salt.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May God's favor always rest on you, and make you a blessing of love to more people. Amen!
